sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the continuity in nature stems from the root of the line (kav) which originates from the Ein Sof before the tzimtzum, and that this root, from the hidden delight, unites the infinite and the finite, allowing the revelation of infinity within the bounds of nature.

translations.translation: And this can be explained based on what is stated in the Continuation of 5666,
that this aspect of continuity in the conduct of nature
(although nature is from the Divine vitality that is clothed within the creations,
and the vitality clothed within the creations is limited vitality,
as mentioned above)
is because the root of the vitality clothed within the creations is
(not from the vessels,
but rather)
from the light of the line (kav),
whose root is from the Ein Sof that preceded the tzimtzum.
And as explained in many places
that the root of the vessels is from the tzimtzum itself,
and the root of the line (kav) is from the Ein Sof that preceded the tzimtzum
(except that it is drawn down through the tzimtzum),
as stated in Etz Chayim
that after the tzimtzum, He drew down from the Ein Sof a single straight line from the light of its circle.
And behold, it is known
that this that the line (kav) pierced the darkness of the tzimtzum,
and every piercing is due to intensity,
is because the root of its drawing down is from the hidden delight,
which is above the light that shone
(in revelation)
before the tzimtzum.

And based on this, it can be explained that this superiority in the revelation of the power of the Ein Sof that is revealed through the continuity in the conduct of nature, relative to the revelation of the Ein Sof through miracles,
is,
because the light before the tzimtzum is limited in the aspect of the boundless,
and it is impossible for its revelation to be within the boundary of the worlds.
Therefore,
the revelation of the encompassing light
[which is the revelation of the light before the tzimtzum]
from which the root of miracles derives,
is through the overturning of nature,
the nullification of nature
(boundary)
of the world.
And the light of the line (kav), from which comes the continuity in the conduct of nature,
since its root is from the hidden delight,
it includes and connects the two opposites of the boundless and boundary.
Therefore,
the revelation of the boundless
(eternity)
that comes from the light of the line (kav) is also within boundary
(nature).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two types of miracles—those above nature and those clothed in nature—are two modes of revealing the Ein Sof's boundlessness that is beyond being clothed in boundary, with the superiority of miracles clothed in nature being that they demonstrate the Ein Sof's rule over nature itself.

translations.translation: e)
And behold, based on the above
(section d)
that even the continuity in the conduct of nature is through the drawing down of the revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, which is above the worlds,
and the superiority of miracles is that through them is drawn down the revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless itself, which is beyond being clothed in boundary,
it can be said,
that the two types of miracles,
miracles above nature and miracles clothed in nature,
are two modes in the revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, which is beyond being clothed in boundary.
And based on this,
that which was stated above
(section c)
that the superiority of miracles clothed in nature is that the revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, becomes clothed within the boundary of the world itself,
is,
that in miracles there is also the aspect and superiority of the conduct of nature,
and the superiority of miracles clothed in nature regarding the aspect of the miracles themselves
(revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, which is beyond being clothed)
is,
that in them it is revealed that this Ein Sof, the boundless
(which is beyond being clothed)
rules and dominates over nature in such a way that even nature itself becomes according to His will
(the second explanation in the aforementioned section).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in miracles above nature, the nullification of nature's existence reveals the Ein Sof's dominion over nature's very essence, whereas in miracles clothed in nature, the dominion is only over nature's mode of conduct, corresponding to the difference between the essence of will and its illumination.

translations.translation: And similarly, this is also regarding miracles above nature,
that the superiority of these miracles is also that the miracles are in revelation, and also that this—that the Ein Sof, the boundless, rules and dominates over nature—is revealed more
(in one particular aspect)
in miracles above nature.
For in miracles clothed in nature,
where nature remains in existence,
the dominion of the Ein Sof over nature is
(only)
that the manner of nature's conduct is according to His will,
and in miracles above nature,
where nature is nullified from its existence,
the dominion of the Ein Sof over nature is over its very existence.
And it can be said,
that the difference between the types of miracles in their root is,
that in miracles clothed in nature, it is a revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, as it relates to and gives place to boundary.
Therefore,
relative to the revelation of this light,
the existence of nature
(the boundary)
exists, except that the boundary is according to the will of the Ein Sof, the boundless.
And in miracles above nature, it is a revelation of the Ein Sof, the boundless, as it is above the aspect of boundary,
therefore,
relative to the revelation of this light,
nature is nullified from its existence.
[And analogous to what is explained elsewhere
regarding the matter of will and intellect
[for will and intellect are a parable for the encompassing light
(the root of miracles)
and the filling light
(the root of nature)],
that this that the will is drawn into the intellect and acts upon it so that there will be a reason for the will,
is only the illumination of the will,
but the essence of the will is not drawn into the intellect,
there is no reason for the will].
